children: British retailer John Lewis Partnership said its first-half loss deepened and it warned it was cautious on the current period, as an uncertain economic and geopolitical landscape weighs on customers.

The UK's largest employee-owned business, which runs John Lewis department stores and the upmarket Waitrose supermarket chain, tends to make most of its profit in the six months from August to January, which includes peak Christmas trading.
For the six months to August 1, it made a loss before tax and exceptional items of £89 million pounds, compared to a loss of £34 million for the same period in 2025. Sales grew 2% to £6.3 billion.

The period included a rise in fuel prices triggered by the start of the Iran War in February. John Lewis said it had seen weaker demand for larger discretionary purchases in general merchandise over those months.

"Our first-half results reflect our continued investment in our transformation, a more challenging trading environment and the increased costs of doing business," chairman Jason Tarry said in a statement on Thursday.

While UK data over the summer showed some signs of strength, economists have warned on the country's vulnerability to high inflation from the Iran war and the uncertainty for households ahead of the new finance minister's first budget on October 28.
Tarry said the group was now focused on Christmas, for which it was well set-up.
